summary.value: The Pyncheon is a rare true bantam, meaning it has no large fowl version. It was bred in the northeastern United States from birds thought to have come over from the Netherlands or Belgium, and it is one of the older American bantams. Nathaniel Hawthorne kept the breed and wrote its birds into The House of the Seven Gables. The Pyncheon wears a small crest behind a single comb that often bends into an S shape, and most birds show a Mille Fleur type of spotted pattern. Hens are fair layers of small white eggs and go broody often, so they make willing mothers. The birds are friendly and docile, but like most bantams they fly well, so a covered run helps. The American Bantam Association recognizes the breed, while the American Poultry Association does not.
